question: Should AI safety events become a host-owned extension of the canonical audit/diagnostics system, or should OpenClaw establish a separate public plugin event subsystem with its own trust, persistence, and compatibility contract?
rationale: The choice determines who can assert trusted safety findings, which persistent ledger owns operator history, and whether a new public Plugin SDK contract is supportable; automation cannot safely choose those permanent boundaries.

options.title: Narrow and redesign
options.body: Keep the taxonomy idea, but move provenance into an injected host capability and extend the canonical audit ledger before adding the plugin API or UI.

options.title: Sponsor a dedicated subsystem
options.body: Accept a separate safety channel only after defining versioning, host-resolved plugin authorization, durable storage, lifecycle startup, Gateway broadcast, and upgrade guarantees.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or pause the PR if no owner can sponsor the long-term security and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Narrow and redesign
recommendation.body: Keep the taxonomy idea, but move provenance into an injected host capability and extend the canonical audit ledger before adding the plugin API or UI.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core product architecture, Plugin SDK compatibility, Gateway protocol, and security ownership rather than belonging to one narrow module.
